solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise a business centre for greed

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise sharply
the City is London's financial district, so a city stands for a business centre

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a financial district for its avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, the original 'business centre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping, plundering avarice, a straightforward synonym of greed.

clue.text: Look forward to something saucy

definitions.meaning: a piquant sauce or pickle served with food

explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy in prospect is one sense; a tangy condiment such as chutney is the other.

clue.text: Letter marvellous to read out — in which there are no clear views?

definitions.text: in which there are no clear views?

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the letter's name and the word are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the letter P followed by super, meaning marvellous

explanation.surface: A wonderful letter is recited in a place with poor visibility.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the letter P and 'super' give the hyphenated word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick yellowish London fog, through which nothing can be seen clearly.

clue.text: After cold, a cut is unfortunately burning

indicators.note: the rest follows the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: unluckily arranged, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Following frostbite, a wound sadly stings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges A CUT IS into AUSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic substances corrode tissue, so they are burning in the chemical sense.

clue.text: Close to blunt instrument, something sharp

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the word blunt supplies its final letter

parts.note: a horn is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Next to a blunt weapon lies something pointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' suggests a weapon but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon's grave fight on the counter

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: a bar is the counter where drinks are served
a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: An ancient burial site is the scene of a brawl at a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the fight after the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is an ancient burial mound, as raised over Anglo-Saxon chieftains.

clue.text: Rug in this fashion possibly could be corrugated

indicators.note: the letters might be rearranged into the target word

parts.note: added to the answer's letters, it makes up the fodder

explanation.surface: A carpet in this design might be ridged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus RUG is an anagram of CORRUGATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative style of the 1920s and 30s, with bold geometric shapes; fashion means style here.

clue.text: Character of Milne and Eliot family

parts.note: Roo is Kanga's baby in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh
the poet T. S. Eliot

explanation.surface: A literary personality bridging two authors and their family.
explanation.definitionFit: Roots are one's ancestry, family origins.

clue.text: Message about hopeless case in smart Aleck

indicators.note: the message goes around the other letters

parts.note: a wire is a telegram, a message

indicators.note: in a mess, so the letters of case are jumbled

explanation.surface: A note about a lost cause found inside a know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopeless' turns CASE into SEAC, which 'about' places in WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all who thinks himself clever, a synonym of smart alec.

clue.text: These might get dropped at the end of the day — oh dear!

definitions.text: These might get dropped at the end of the day

definitions.meaning: a mild British exclamation of annoyance

explanation.definitionFit: Women's underpants are taken off at night; the word is also a British cry of exasperation.

clue.text: Post-WWI coalition saluting a foe, one failing

indicators.note: something failing has gone wrong, so the letters of the fodder are disordered

explanation.surface: A wartime alliance greets an enemy, and one member falters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' signals the anagram of SALUTING A FOE ONE; it also hints at the body's real fate.
explanation.definitionFit: The international body founded in 1920 after the First World War, a forerunner of the United Nations.

clue.text: Figure on endless beach finds dock

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
without its end, so the final letter of the word for beach is dropped

parts.note: the shore is the beach
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A shape spotted on a long beach discovers a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a noun, a harbour, but is the verb meaning cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail or wages is to cut it back, making it less long.

clue.text: Porcelain tea cups besides

indicators.note: to cup is to hold in the hands, so the word for tea encloses the other piece

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
else means besides or in addition

explanation.surface: Fine china teacups set out alongside something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like teaware but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a celebrated eighteenth-century English porcelain, named after the London district where it was made.

clue.text: In condition, muscle to behold

indicators.note: placed first, it tells us the muscle goes inside the condition

parts.note: a state is a condition
a pec is a pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A fit body in good shape is something to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to watch an event, so to look on or behold.

clue.text: Broadcast can do with aria, though not Beethoven's Sixth, Pastoral

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are mixed
removing the following letter from the fodder

parts.note: the sixth letter of Beethoven is O

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast handles an aria, unlike Beethoven's Sixth, his Pastoral Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Sixth' looks like the symphony nicknamed 'Pastoral', but is the letter O, removed before 'Broadcast' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadian means idyllically rural, from Arcadia, the shepherds' paradise of Greek myth.

clue.text: Different — Bathsheba, Jezebel or Delilah, might you say?

indicators.note: asks for the words spoken, here in an aitch-dropping accent

parts.note: each is a biblical temptress, a hot her, which dropping both aitches gives 'ot 'er

explanation.surface: Three notorious women of the Bible, offered as examples of something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: Each seductress is a 'hot her'; spoken with dropped aitches, 'ot 'er gives the letters entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same, a synonym of different.

clue.text: One getting stick after lessening of speed, a great blow

indicators.note: the pieces come after the shortened word
the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: to hurry is to speed
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A slowing walker leans on a stick, a hard blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm, a wind that blows fiercely.

clue.text: Going on and on relentlessly at first, then walking casually

indicators.note: the opening letter of relentlessly

parts.note: ambling is strolling at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Someone presses on, then saunters along.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling talk is long-winded and wanders without end.

clue.text: Every second in day a drag, oh I'm so frustrated!

indicators.note: take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on from the run of words

explanation.surface: A tedious day prompts a cry of exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: From DAYADRAGOH, the even letters give the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a groan of exasperation, voicing frustration.

clue.text: Good Lord in the sky?

explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise and also the sky above, the celestial vault.

clue.text: Money, simply fine stuff

parts.note: cash is money
mere means nothing more than, as simply does

explanation.surface: Money alone is a lovely thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is fabric here, not things in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a soft, fine wool fabric from goat hair; stuff is an old word for woven cloth.

clue.text: Are immaculate walls in Muslim tower?

indicators.note: surrounds, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: in mint condition means immaculate

explanation.surface: Asks whether a mosque tower has spotless walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: German heavyweight bust container ship

parts.note: a bra holds the bust
HMS, His Majesty's Ship, prefixes Royal Navy ship names

explanation.surface: A big German boxer breaks up a cargo vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a verb but is the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms, a towering German composer, a heavyweight of music.

clue.text: Equipment nicked by gang robber

indicators.note: taken by, so the equipment ends up held inside the gang

parts.note: a band is a gang
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Gear stolen by a criminal outfit belonging to a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' suggests theft, but the equipment is just held inside the gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, an outlaw who robs travellers.

clue.text: Plant that's cold, short of summit

indicators.note: in a down clue the summit is the top letter, which is dropped

parts.note: winter is the cold season

explanation.surface: A plant that suffers frost, not reaching the mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' means bury, not a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, to plant it in the earth.

clue.text: I appreciate that rule must be reversed for African city

parts.note: ta is informal British thanks

indicators.note: says the word for rule is read backwards

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: A grateful voice insists a regulation be overturned for a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port city in northern Morocco on the Strait of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Volunteering force showing character in Greece

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, always spoken of with the article in front
TA is the abbreviation for the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers show their mettle in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve, is always 'the TA', so the article comes with it: no clue word supplies it separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet; character means a written letter.

clue.text: When both lungs are filled, coincidentally

definitions.meaning: a playful literal sense: both lungs drawing in a single inhalation
at the same moment, said almost simultaneously

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means saying two things at once; taken literally it is one inhalation filling both lungs.

clue.text: Loud cheer finally, one having cut rent

indicators.note: the pieces cut into the tear, ending up inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a gash

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word cheer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rowdy celebration closes, with a tenant having had rent reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is a tear, not a payment; 'Loud' describes colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud colours or clothes are showy and tasteless, the sense of gaudy, brash.

clue.text: Hot filling in hot dogs, perhaps — for cats!

indicators.note: the H fills the inside of the other word

parts.note: overheated dogs pant, so they might be called panters
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spicy sausage filling meant for felines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dogs' are not sausages but panting animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Panthers are big cats, leopards or jaguars.
